newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port seen nearing container capacity in 97.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port seen nearing container capacity in 97.

text.p: A sharp rise in container traffic at Sri Lanka's main port of Colombo this year could see south Asia's trans-shipment hub nearing its capacity in 1997, port officials said on Wednesday.
"At the rate of 129,000 containers a month we could handle 1.5 million containers next year, very close to our capacity," a senior port official said.

The port, with a capacity of 1.6 million containers, handled 1.2 million containers in the 11 months to the end of November, with 129,000 units handled in that month alone, the highest monthly throughput, he said.
"We expect 128,000 containers in December so we could do something like 1.35 million units for the year, which is exactly 300,000 containers more than 1995, a roughly 28 percent increase," he said.
The increase was mainly in trans-shipment traffic, he said.
Trans-shipment is when a vessel discharges cargo at an intermediate port and the goods are loaded into another ship bound for the final destination.
"Some months, we did 55 percent more of trans-shipment than the same month the year before," said the official, who declined to be identified.
The sharp rise in trans-shipment traffic came after the realignment of container shipping alliances in the middle of the year, port officials said.
The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), which runs Colombo port, is holding talks with a consortium led by the Peninsula & Oriental Shipping Co to set up a new container terminal to expand capacity.

The project is estimated to cost up to $1 billion and will take 10 years to build. It will see the development of the southern part of the port with at least another six deep-draft berths, for fifth and sixth generation ships, with a capacity of two million containers a year.
The port has cracked down on labour problems and plans new tariffs to improve services and attract bigger and more modern vessels, port officials said.
